Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

r4lineups 2.3.0 (development)

Breaking changes

  • make_dpp() now computes the deviation from perfect performance as Smith, Lampinen, Wells, Smalarz and Mackovichova (2019) define it: DPP(c) = 1 - Culprit(c) + Innocent(c) at each ROC operating point, averaged over the operating points (their Equation 2). The previous statistic, 1 - AUC(observed) / AUC(perfect) over the observed false-ID range, was a different quantity under the same name, and it cited an unrelated paper. On a single operating point with culprit rate .8 and innocent-suspect rate .1, the old function returned .6; the published measure is .3. The new version reproduces Smith et al.’s Table 4 (.864 and .816). The return value now has dpp, dpp_by_point and best_point in place of auc_observed, auc_perfect, auc_gap, perfect_roc and max_fa. Optional alpha and beta arguments give their weighted Equation 3.
  • compare_dpp() now bootstraps the difference in average DPP (stratified by target presence within each procedure) and returns its standard error and a percentile interval, with a print method. plot_dpp() plots DPP at each operating point; plot_dpp_comparison() overlays two procedures and loses its layout argument. plot_dpp() arguments are now show_mean, show_chance and show_dpp.

New features

  • Every analysis that uses target-absent lineups gains an innocent_suspect argument: "designated", "estimated" (filler IDs / lineup size), or "auto" (the default). The app’s Data tab has a matching control. See the bug fix below.
  • make_cacdata(), make_cac(), ppv_by_confidence(), ppv_range_by_confidence() and make_ppv_range() gain base_rate. Count-based accuracy, the Mickes (2015) definition, stays the default, but it equals the probability of guilt only when the target-present and target-absent samples are the same size: with HR = .6 and FAR = .1 it gives .857, .923 or .667 for TP:TA splits of 100:100, 200:100 and 100:300. These functions now say so in a message when the arms differ. base_rate = 0.5 computes accuracy from the hit and false-ID rates instead, which gives .857 for all three; other values apply Bayes’ rule at that prior. The rate-based CAC standard error is a delta-method approximation. Existing results are unchanged.

Bug fixes

  • make_rocdata() and make_utility_curves() took a confidence criterion from every response, rejections included. The extra criteria only duplicated existing operating points, so the ROC path and partial AUC were unaffected, but averages over points were reweighted by how rejection confidence happened to be coded. Changing only the rejection confidences (from 0 to values between 51 and 99) moved average DPP from .417 to .647 and equal-variance z-ROC d’ from 1.879 to 1.398. The criteria are now the confidence levels of the responses that can move an operating point: target-present suspect IDs, plus target-absent suspect IDs with a designated suspect or filler IDs without one. Both codings now give DPP .475 and d’ 1.757. Results change for data in which rejections or filler IDs carry confidence levels that no counted ID uses; lineup_example is unaffected. make_rocdata(), make_dpp() and make_utility_curves() gain thresholds to set the criteria, and make_rocdata() and make_dpp() return the criteria used. compare_dpp() and the fit_sdt_roc() bootstrap reuse the full-sample criteria in every replicate, so that all replicates estimate the same average.

  • Target presence coded 0/1, which the validator accepts, broke the bootstraps in compare_pauc() (an error) and fit_sdt_roc(), where every replicate failed silently and the intervals were NA with n_successful = 0. Both now resample 0/1 and logical coding identically. fit_sdt_roc() also warns when bootstrap samples fail, giving the number and the first error.

  • func_size_report() bootstrapped functional size, 1/p, and boot.ci() silently dropped the resamples with no target choices, where it is infinite. With one target choice among 30 mock witnesses, 353 of 1,000 resamples were dropped and the percentile interval was [10, 30]. The bootstrap now resamples p and inverts its limits, which gives the same percentile and BCa intervals when every resample is finite and an unbounded upper limit when it is not ([10, Inf] here). The result gains an exact interval (inverted Clopper-Pearson, [5.81, 1185.44] here) and n_infinite, the number of resamples without target choices. The app’s Bias & size tab shows both, and displays infinite limits instead of leaving them blank.

  • standardize_lineup_data() kept only the columns it maps, so it dropped suspect_pos and lineup_member. A designated suspect who was never chosen then fell back to the filler estimate after standardization (false-ID rate .10 instead of 0), and effective-size-corrected PPV lost its member choices (.833 instead of .50 when target-absent choices fall on one member). Every column it does not map is now carried through unchanged.

  • compare_multid() differenced the two bootstrap matrices row by row. The conditions are independent samples, but fits made with the same seed have correlated draws, so the standard error collapsed. Comparing counts (60, 25, 15, 10, 30, 60) with (60, 27, 13, 10, 30, 60), both fitted with seed 1, gave d’(GFp) a standard error of .014 and p < .0001; the correct values are .347 and .86. Identical inputs gave a zero-width interval. The standard error is now the square root of the sum of the two bootstrap variances, and the interval comes from randomly re-paired draws. compare_multid() gains seed.

  • get_face_landmarks() failed with every current MediaPipe release. The image was read into R and passed back as an int32 array, which OpenCV and MediaPipe reject, and the function used mediapipe.solutions.face_mesh, which current MediaPipe no longer has. The image now stays a uint8 numpy array, and when solutions is absent the MediaPipe Tasks FaceLandmarker is used. Its model is downloaded once to tools::R_user_dir("r4lineups", "cache"). Both routes return the 478-point mesh (468 face points plus 10 iris points); the documentation said 468. check_python_deps() now records in a "face_mesh" attribute whether landmarks can actually be extracted, not only whether MediaPipe imports. An opt-in test (R4LINEUPS_RUN_FACE=true) exercises the whole path.

  • In the app’s Bias & size tab, ticking “Small-sample corrected E’” changed the reported estimate but left its intervals on the plug-in estimator, so the value box could show a corrected E’ with a plug-in interval that did not contain it. esize_boot_dist() gains unbiased = FALSE, which bootstraps the corrected estimator (dropping, with a warning, resamples where it is unbounded). The app now bootstraps the corrected E’ when it reports it, and lists the plug-in estimate with its own normal-theory and bootstrap intervals on separately labelled rows.

  • Target-absent data with a designated innocent suspect who was never chosen were treated as having no designated suspect, so the false-ID rate was estimated from filler IDs instead of being zero. With 100 target-absent lineups, 60 filler IDs and no suspect IDs, the ROC reached a false-ID rate of .10 instead of 0. "auto" now treats the lineups as designated when any target-absent row is a suspect ID or the data carry a non-missing suspect_pos column (as simulate_lineup_data() output and lineup_example do). Otherwise it falls back to the filler estimate with a message. Bootstraps (compare_pauc(), fit_sdt_roc(), bootstrap_anri(), compare_anri()), make_calibration_by_condition(), make_utility_difference(), ppv_range_by_confidence() and the make_multid() confidence breakdown now resolve the design once on the full data, so a resample that happens to contain no suspect IDs no longer switches estimator.

  • ppv_by_confidence() dropped every confidence bin that contained no target-absent trials, and with it that bin’s guilty-suspect IDs, so both the bin and the overall PPV were wrong. With 90 guilty IDs at confidence 100 and all target-absent responses at 50, the overall PPV was .50 instead of .909. Such bins are now kept, with no innocent-suspect IDs (PPV 1) and an NA error rate and effective size. Only bins empty in both arms are dropped. make_ppv_range() and its plots inherit the fix.

  • boot_winter_2ht(method = "bca") failed with a dimnames error, because the interval matrix was transposed into the wrong shape, and even before that its acceleration was fixed at 0, so the “BCa” interval was only bias-corrected. The acceleration is now the jackknife estimate (one refit per non-empty response cell, weighted by its count), the bias correction handles ties and stays finite, and both methods return a parameters x (Lower, Upper) matrix.

  • The posterior means reported by func_size_bayes(), diag_ratio_T_bayes() and diag_ratio_T_bayes_compare() were averages of reciprocal draws. When the relevant Beta posterior has shape a <= 1 (for example, no suspect choices under the Jeffreys prior), the true mean is infinite and the average never settled: it was about 11 million, 3 million and 36 million for 10^3, 10^4 and 10^5 draws of the same functional size. The means are now computed exactly, (a + b - 1) / (a - 1) for 1/p, and are Inf when they do not exist. Print methods say so; a difference of two infinite means is NA. Medians, intervals and threshold probabilities are unchanged.

  • compare_pauc() overstated partial AUC whenever the ROC had a vertical segment, that is, when a confidence level added correct IDs but no false IDs. Its integrator kept only the upper endpoint of each such segment, so the next sloping segment started from too high a correct-ID rate. A curve through (0, 0), (0, .5), (.1, .5) and (.1, 1) has area .05; compare_pauc() reported .075 while make_rocdata() reported .05. Both now use one internal integrator that keeps every endpoint and interpolates within the segment that crosses the cutoff, and their results agree. The compare_pauc() bootstrap and simulate_power_analysis() use the same integrator.

r4lineups 2.2.0 (2026-10-28)

Breaking changes

  • The first argument of esize_T(), esize_m(), i_esize_T(), gen_linevec(), lineup_prop_tab(), allfoilbias(), datacheck3(), esize_T_boot(), esize_T_bayes() and esize_T_ci_n() is renamed from lineup_table to lineup_tab, so that it no longer collides with the new lineup_table() function (see below). Code that calls these functions positionally is unaffected; code that passes the argument by name (e.g. esize_T(lineup_table = x)) must be updated to esize_T(lineup_tab = x).

  • simulate_power_analysis() now performs an actual power analysis and its arguments have changed accordingly. It takes d_prime_null (the comparison condition), n_bootstrap, lineup_size, seed and verbose; the former stat_function argument is replaced by test_function, which takes two dataframes and returns a p-value. The returned columns are now sample_size, power, power_se, mean_effect, sd_effect and n_valid. See the bug-fix entry below for why this was necessary.

  • lineup_example has been regenerated and now has 1400 rows rather than 200, with lineup_member and suspect_pos columns. Numeric results computed from it will differ from previous versions.

Bug fixes

  • simulate_power_analysis() computed power as the proportion of simulations in which the pAUC exceeded zero. A partial area under a curve is always positive, so that proportion was always exactly 1, for every sample size and every effect size, and the resulting power curve was a flat line at the top of the plot. Power is now the proportion of simulated studies in which a test of the difference between two conditions reaches significance, using compare_pauc() by default. The single test covering this function was skipped and additionally asserted a field the function never returned, so the fault could not have been caught; it has been replaced with tests that run.

  • make_roc(), make_cac(), make_rac(), make_fullroc(), make_calibration() and compute_dpp() set $plot to NULL when called with show_plot = FALSE, so suppressing display also destroyed the plot object. result$plot was then NULL and nothing could be drawn from it — the cause of several “the plot does not show” reports. The plot is now always built, and show_plot controls only whether it is displayed immediately, which is what its documentation always said it did.

  • compare_pauc() chose its default region of integration as the larger of the two conditions’ maximum false-ID rates. Since neither curve extends past its own maximum and no extrapolation is performed, the curve that stopped sooner was integrated over a smaller interval than the other, so the two “partial areas” covered different regions and were not comparable. In testing, this understated a real difference by around 14%. The default is now the largest region both curves attain, a message reports it when the two differ, and an explicit max_false_id_rate beyond either curve’s reach now warns.

  • make_fullroc() and make_fullroc_data() now report that the default order = "diagnosticity" is optimistically biased. Because the ordering of evidence categories is estimated from the same data used to compute the area, data containing no signal at all return a mean AUC of roughly 0.65 at 100 lineups per arm, 0.60 at 200 and 0.55 at 1000, against a true value of 0.5. A-priori ordering is unbiased at every sample size tested. The default is unchanged, since it is the ordering Smith et al. describe, but a message now points to order = "apriori" for inferential use.

  • fit_winter_2ht() failed with non-finite finite-difference value when the data contained almost no lineup rejections. The detect-absence parameter dA is identified by rejections, so the likelihood is nearly flat without them. It now stops with a message naming the actual problem and the likely cause — a decision criterion so liberal that witnesses never reject. compare_models() had silently omitted the 2-HT model in this situation, so every downstream section that referred to it produced no output.

  • format_comparison_table(format = "markdown") produced a table that rendered as a single run-on paragraph. It returns a knitr_kable object, which is a character vector with one element per line, and the vignette printed it with cat(x) — joining the lines with spaces. The vignette now uses cat(x, sep = "\n") and the return value is documented as line-per-element. The markdown and latex forms also called kable() without row.names = FALSE, so row names inherited from the named parameter vectors (“dP”, “dA”, …) appeared as a spurious unlabelled first column.

  • plot_2ht_parameters() rejected winter_2ht_boot objects, although its documentation offered confidence intervals “if bootstrapped”. It now accepts them and draws the bootstrap percentile intervals. For a plain fit it still draws normal approximations, but clamped to [0, 1]: all four parameters are probabilities, and on lineup_example the interval for b previously ran to -0.023.

  • plot.esize_T_bayes() packed the credible interval into the plot title using an embedded newline, producing a two-line 74-character title laid out as a single text grob — the usual cause of a heading running off the top of a rendered figure. The interval is now a subtitle. The other five Bayesian plot methods were checked and none had the same fault.

  • Effective size is no longer referred to eponymously as “Tredoux effective size” in documentation, printed output or plot labels; it is now “effective size” with the citation (Tredoux, 1998). Affects esize_T(), i_esize_T(), esize_T_ci_n() and the esize_T_bayes() family.

  • fit_max_sdt() left bootstrap replicates that failed to converge as NA rows in boot_params without recording how many, so sd(fit$boot_params[, 1]) returned NA unexplained. It now reports boot_n_used and boot_n_failed, warns when more than 10% fail, and errors rather than returning meaningless intervals if all of them do. Its documentation also gained a “Provenance” section crediting the R scripts of A. M. Smith from which the implementation follows, and a “Relation to Smith’s scripts” section explaining why estimates differ: this function uses five mutually exclusive response cells, whereas those scripts fit total target-present choices alongside culprit identifications, counting the latter twice.

  • install_r4lineups_python() failed with reticulate’s opaque Suitable Python installation for creating a venv not found when python_version named a version not present on the machine, without saying how to obtain one. It now checks first, reports which versions it did find, and gives the reticulate::install_python() call needed.

  • Vignette.Rmd drew random numbers – simulated ages and every bootstrap – without a seed, so its output changed on every build. Seeded once in setup.

  • make_bayes_curves() now warns when a response category has no observations in one arm. The likelihood ratio is then unbounded and the prior-posterior curve is pinned flat at 0 or 1, which looks like a plotting fault rather than a data problem.

  • The member-level branch of the effective-size calculation in ppv_by_confidence() counted rejections as a lineup position and did not tabulate over all positions, so unchosen members were dropped. This branch was previously unreachable, as no dataset supplied a lineup_member column.

  • plot_lineup_bias_distribution() and plot_esize_distribution() no longer draw ragged histograms with structural gaps. A bootstrapped lineup proportion is a count over a fixed denominator, so the replicates fall on a lattice with spacing 1/n; binning them at a fixed 30 bins left bins that contained no attainable value empty regardless of the data, and made bins that straddled two attainable values twice as tall as their neighbours. The bin width is now chosen to match the lattice, giving one bar per attainable value. Estimates that are effectively continuous still use 30 bins. Both functions gained bins and binwidth arguments for explicit control.

  • plot_fullroc() labelled the plot "Ordering method: " with nothing after it when given the output of make_fullroc(), because the ordering method is recorded at $order_used on a make_fullroc_data() object but at $summary$order_method on a make_fullroc() object. Both shapes are now accepted, and an object carrying neither raises an informative error.

  • plot() now works on the ROC and CAC objects. make_rocdata(), make_cacdata() and make_fullroc_data() returned unclassed lists, so plot(x) dispatched to plot.default() and failed; the package registered print methods for these objects but no plot methods. Added plot.lineup_roc(), plot.lineup_cac(), plot.lineup_fullroc() and methods for the corresponding *_data classes, all reusing the existing make_roc_gg(), make_cac_gg() and plot_fullroc() builders.

  • install_r4lineups_python() pinned no Python version, so reticulate could select an interpreter newer than any for which TensorFlow publishes wheels, and the install failed partway through with No matching distribution found for tensorflow. It now checks the interpreter before downloading anything and stops with an actionable message, and gained a python_version argument for building the virtual environment from a supported interpreter.

New features

  • New make_multid() implements Lee and Penrod’s (2019) Multi-d’ model. From target-present and target-absent lineup data (trial-level or counts) it computes d’(GI), d’(GFp), d’(IFa), d’(FaFp) and d’(RaRp), the TP and TA lineup-bias indices, the criterion and the diagnosticity ratio, with optional bootstrap intervals and a cumulative breakdown by confidence. Because the model uses total filler rates, a fair lineup does not give d’(IFa) = 0, so the result also reports the d’(IFa) a perfectly fair lineup would give at the observed rejection rate. compare_multid() compares two conditions, and plot.multid() draws the decomposition of d’(GI), the indices, or the indices by confidence. The tests reproduce Lee and Penrod’s Tables 3, 4 and

    1. See vignette("multid_model").

  • esize_T() gained an unbiased argument. The default (FALSE) is the plug-in estimator as before, so no existing result changes. unbiased = TRUE applies the small-sample correction N(N-1) / sum(o(o-1)). The plug-in form is biased downward, by approximately k(k-1)/(N + k - 1): a perfectly fair six-person lineup assessed with 50 choices returns about 5.47 rather than 6, and with 20 choices about 4.87. The correction removes essentially all of it in simulation, at a variance cost that disappears by about 100 choices. The bias, the evidence and the choice between the two forms are documented in ?esize_T, with cross-references from ?esize_m and ?esize_T_ci_n.

  • New classify_lineup_choices() derives identification outcomes (suspect ID, foil ID, rejection) from the raw record of which lineup member each witness chose. Lineup data should record the member chosen, with the collapsed label derived from it rather than stored in its place, because foils are not interchangeable and a foil nobody ever chooses is what makes a lineup unfair.

  • simulate_lineup_data() gained a foil_bias argument, giving each foil its own mean memory strength so that foils differ in plausibility rather than being drawn from a common distribution. The default (NULL) preserves the previous behaviour exactly.

  • simulate_lineup_data() now returns lineup_member (the position chosen, 0 for a rejection) and suspect_pos alongside identification. The chosen position was already computed internally and discarded.

  • plot.power_analysis() shows a Monte Carlo interval around the power curve, so that apparent dips between adjacent points can be recognised as simulation noise, and returns the ggplot object invisibly for further modification.

  • homog_diag() and homog_diag_boot() now report the diagnosticity ratio and a confidence interval for each lineup pair, not just the pooled mean and the chi-square. The chi-square is Cochran’s Q, which measures how far the k ratios lie from their pooled value; that is a different question from whether the pooled ratio differs from 1, and the two can disagree sharply. Ratios of 6.0, 1.0 and 0.44 give Q = 45.6 (p < .0001) while pooling to 1.06, because they cancel on the log scale — an output that reads as “highly significant, but no diagnosticity” unless the per-pair values are visible. Both functions now print a note stating whether the ratios are heterogeneous and, when they are, that the pooled estimate averages quantities that are not estimating a common parameter and should not be reported on its own. The returned list gained a heterogeneous flag, and homog_diag_boot() gained df and p_value; the parameters element now carries d, ln_d, var_lnd, wi, lower and upper alongside the existing cell counts. Both functions gained a conf.level argument, which also sets the level for homog_diag_boot()’s percentile intervals (default 0.95, unchanged from the previous hard-coded value).

  • Added lineup_table(), which tabulates lineup choices across all k positions so that null foils — members no mock witness chose — appear as explicit zeroes rather than being silently dropped by table(). Its print method names the null foils and marks the nominated suspect. The result inherits from table, so it can be passed to esize_m(), esize_T() and the other table-taking functions unchanged.

Shiny app

  • The app bundled with run_r4lineups_app() has been rebuilt on bslib, with one module per analysis. Every number it shows now comes from an exported r4lineups function; the app’s own copy of the Malpass effective-size formula is gone.
  • The ROC, CAC, full ROC, pAUC, EIG and PPV analyses previously assumed a six-person lineup whatever the data. Lineup size is now set on a new Data tab, which loads one confidence-based data set (built-in or uploaded) for all of these analyses and lets any column define two groups to compare.
  • New tabs cover the diagnosticity ratio and its homogeneity test, Lee and Penrod’s Multi-d’ model, and calibration and decision analyses (ANRI, DPP, expected utility, Bayesian and BREE curves, RAC). The fairness tab adds the binomial test against chance, bootstrap distributions, functional size and the corrected E’.
  • Bootstrap and posterior analyses now run when Run analysis is clicked rather than on every keystroke, take a seed, and are computed once, so a table’s interval and the plotted distribution come from the same draws. Messages and warnings from the package are shown beside the results.
  • Every table downloads as CSV and every plot as PNG. “Download ROC/CAC data” previously wrote an .rds file.
  • The app no longer counts sessions on disk or fetches download totals from CRAN and GitHub at start-up.
  • The face similarity tab now includes the Python setup that used to be the first tab, and is hidden when reticulate is unavailable.
  • run_r4lineups_app() checks that shiny, bslib and DT are installed. bslib and shinytest2 join Suggests; shinyWidgets and jsonlite leave.

Output and documentation

  • make_racdata() labels response-time bins in plain notation, e.g. [2390,4810] rather than [2.39e+03,4.81e+03].

  • ROC and CAC print methods now say "Plot: use plot(x), or save the object and extract x$plot" rather than the cryptic "Plot available in $plot".

  • print.lineup_roc() and print.lineup_fullroc() now report "Target-present trials (N)" rather than "Target-present lineups", which read as a count of lineups when it is a count of witnesses.

  • make_roc_gg() now names the ROC variant in the title, so a partial ROC is not mistaken for a full ROC, and records the data source in the caption. It gained title and data_source arguments.

  • eff_size_per_foils() had no @return documentation at all. Documented that it returns a count of lineup members, so it changes only in whole steps as conf varies and is flat across ranges of conf in which no member’s interval crosses 1/k.

  • eff_size_per_foils() and lineup_boot_allprop() both described conf as “Desired level of alpha”; it is a confidence level. Documented also that lineup_boot_allprop() applies no multiplicity correction across the k intervals it returns.

  • The main vignette has been substantially revised: corrected a typo (line_df$linep_vec), a reference to a nonexistent sample_data dataset, an inverted functional size formula (D/N for N/D), a misstated proportion (“0.14%” for 14%), a misattributed sentence (“He instead proposed” for “Tredoux instead proposed”), and inline code spans that reflowed into a paragraph instead of forming a code chunk. Added sections on null foils, normal-theory versus bootstrap intervals, multiplicity across lineup members, functional size exceeding nominal size, the boot.ci() warnings, the *_data()/wrapper distinction in the ROC and CAC functions, and raw data format for ROC analysis. The homogeneity section now separates the two questions the output answers — whether the k ratios agree with one another (chi-square) and whether the average ratio differs from 1 (interval on the pooled ratio) — with a worked heterogeneous example in which every ratio is diagnostic, followed by a cautionary example in which ratios pointing in opposite directions give a very large chi-square while pooling to roughly 1. The unsupported version 1 face_sim() section has been retired in favour of a pointer to the face similarity vignette, and the vignette closes with a linked index of the other vignettes.

r4lineups 2.1.0 (2026-08-10)

  • Added an explicit authorship and acknowledgements statement recognizing Colin Tredoux and Tamsyn Naylor as authors of the original package; the use of Codex and Claude for code-review, drafting, and debugging support in the latest development cycle; and the published work on which the package’s computational methods rely. Suspected implementation errors should be reported through the GitHub issue tracker.
  • Relicensed the package under the permissive MIT license and added canonical citation metadata for the CRAN and JOSS release.

Wixted lineup-memory model interface

  • Added install_pywitness() and check_pywitness_deps() for an explicit, isolated r4lineups-pywitness virtual environment. Installation uses the immutable archive for audited pyWitness revision e726dcfc09423d0e0ff7f46c8e3a711040293eba; package loading and ordinary CRAN checks never install or initialize it.
  • Added fit_lineup_models() for fair simultaneous lineups, with Independent Observations, Ensemble, Integration, and optional BEST-Rest fits; equal- and unequal-variance paths; zero or estimated shared variance where identified; starting values; optimizer controls; and explicit convergence diagnostics.
  • Results are durable R-native lineup_model_comparison objects with extracted parameters, observed and expected response cells, Pearson statistics, degrees of freedom, p-values, confidence binning, engine metadata, and comparison/fit/ROC plots. No live Python object is retained.
  • The audited engine minimizes Pearson chi-squared. The reported multinomial log likelihood is evaluated at that estimate rather than maximized, so AIC and BIC are deliberately NA rather than invalidly treating it as an MLE.
  • BEST-Rest and Ensemble are reported as scale-equivalent parameterizations and are never counted as independent model-selection evidence. Integration is a historical comparator rather than a recommended default.
  • Added opt-in, three-platform Python tests for wrapper/direct-engine parity, parameter and generating-model recovery, probability partitions, BEST-Rest/Ensemble rescaling, equal/unequal variance, zero/estimated shared variance, sparse confidence cells, and optimizer failure.

r4lineups 2.0.0 (2026-08-08)

Major release: a substantial expansion of the package from the 0.1.x fairness-measure toolkit into a full analysis suite for eyewitness identification research, plus a package-wide statistical audit.

CRAN-readiness and statistical corrections

  • Corrected the legacy fairness estimators and bootstrap helpers: unchosen lineup positions are retained, named count tables are matched by member label, Malpass and Tredoux effective sizes use the documented definitions, Tredoux bootstrap resampling occurs at the witness level, and bootstrap standard errors are the standard deviation of the replicate statistics.
  • Corrected diagnosticity pairing, log-ratio variance, inverse-variance weighting, homogeneity degrees of freedom, and independent TP/TA resampling. pos_list now denotes the actual suspect position for each TP/TA pair (or a two-element TP/TA position pair). Homogeneity inference requires positive suspect-ID cells, as in Tredoux’s uncorrected log-risk procedure.
  • Confidence-based methods now distinguish observed designated innocent-suspect IDs from estimates based on target-absent filler IDs. ROC/CAC/RAC, calibration, PPV, utility, full ROC, EIG, and Bayesian curves no longer add both quantities. With no designated suspect, full ROC/EIG/Bayesian response probabilities split target-absent filler choices into 1 / lineup_size suspect and (lineup_size - 1) / lineup_size filler components.
  • Full-ROC documentation now identifies empirical diagnosticity ordering as an optimistic, sample-dependent ordering. PPV/effective-size, utility false-alarm, fractional calibration/ANRI, saturated single-condition 2-HT, and method-of-moments mSDT assumptions are stated explicitly.
  • Corrected pAUC sorting/interpolation and stratified its bootstrap; corrected unequal-variance z-ROC discriminability and raw-data resampling; fixed binary SDT-GLM validation and the covariance term in summary-level log-beta comparisons.
  • Seed-taking simulation and bootstrap functions now restore the caller’s RNG state. Bootstrap count and confidence arguments are validated and honored, optimizer/bootstrap failures are checked, and numerical/vector edge cases receive explicit errors.
  • Optional Python dependency checks no longer initialize or download a managed Python installation. Face-embedding distances reject missing, non-finite, unequal-length, or zero-norm vectors as appropriate.
  • Added package-wide export-contract and hand-calculation regression tests. All 156 exported functions are referenced by the test suite; functions that require Python, Shiny, lme4, images, or other optional environments have explicit dependency/error-path coverage and opt-in smoke-test exemptions.
  • Reduced evaluated vignette bootstrap/simulation sizes while retaining publication-grade settings in unevaluated examples. Source builds no longer include the audit article PDFs.
  • Corrected the EIG reference to Starns, Cohen, and Rotello (2023).
  • Corrected the lineup-memory simulator: the supplied lowest criterion now controls identification versus rejection, subsequent ordered criteria control confidence, and explicit criteria are preserved. The simulator now implements Independent Observations/MAX, Ensemble, and Integration exactly under its documented independent equal-variance assumptions. "best_rest" remains accepted for compatibility but is identified as a scale-equivalent parameterization of Ensemble.
  • Reframed fit_max_sdt() as a restricted, aggregate, single-criterion, equal-variance Independent-Observations fit estimated by minimum Pearson chi-squared. It is not a maximum-likelihood fit and is not the complete confidence-based Wixted et al. (2018) model.

Major New Features (pyWitness-inspired)

This release implements high-priority features from pyWitness (Mickes et al., 2024), significantly expanding r4lineups’ analytical capabilities for eyewitness identification research.

Model Comparison Framework

  • compare_models(): Unified interface for fitting and comparing multiple models
    • 2-HT (Winter et al., 2022): Multinomial processing tree model
    • EIG (Starns et al., 2023): Expected Information Gain
    • Full ROC (Smith & Yang, 2020): Complete ROC using all responses
  • S3 methods: print(), summary(), plot() for model comparison objects
  • format_comparison_table(): Publication-ready comparison tables
  • Automatic handling of different data requirements across models
  • Side-by-side reporting of non-comparable estimands; AIC/BIC are reported only for the 2-HT likelihood fit and are not used to rank EIG or full-ROC AUC
  • Side-by-side visualizations of model results

pAUC Statistical Comparison

  • compare_pauc(): Rigorous statistical testing of ROC curve differences
  • Z-test framework with bootstrap-based standard errors
  • Automatic false ID rate cutoff handling with interpolation
  • Confidence intervals and effect size calculation (Cohen’s d)
  • Multiple comparison support with adjustment examples
  • Publication-ready side-by-side ROC plots
  • Customizable bootstrap samples and confidence levels

Data Simulation and Power Analysis

  • simulate_lineup_data(): Generate lineup identification data
    • Signal Detection Theory (SDT) model with three distinct decision families:
      • MAX (Independent Observations Model) - Default
      • Ensemble - Best match relative to the lineup mean
      • Integration - Sum memory strengths across all members
    • BEST-REST remains a compatibility parameterization. Its decision variable is k / (k - 1) times Ensemble, so the two fit identically when criteria are rescaled and must not be treated as independent model evidence
    • Based on Wixted et al. (2018) and pyWitness implementations
    • Flexible parameters: d’, criterion, lineup size, confidence levels
    • Optional response time simulation
    • S3 class with print method
  • simulate_power_analysis(): Determine required sample sizes
    • Multiple sample size evaluation
    • Customizable effect measures and comparison types
    • Power curve visualization
  • Full integration with all r4lineups analyses

z-ROC and SDT Parameter Estimation

  • fit_sdt_roc(): Extract d’, criteria, and variance ratio from ROC data
    • Equal and unequal variance SDT models
    • z-transformed ROC analysis following Macmillan & Creelman (2005)
    • Log-linear correction for extreme hit/false alarm rates
    • Bootstrap confidence intervals for parameter estimates
    • Model fit diagnostics (R-squared, residuals)
    • S3 class with print(), plot(), summary() methods
  • Integration with make_rocdata() for seamless workflow
  • Comprehensive examples and documentation
  • 24 unit tests ensuring reliability

Standardized Data Format and Validation

  • validate_lineup_data(): Comprehensive data validation
    • Checks required columns (target_present, identification, confidence)
    • Validates data types and value ranges
    • Detects missing values and invalid identification categories
    • Warns about common data quality issues
    • Strict mode option for error-on-failure behavior
  • standardize_lineup_data(): Convert data from various formats
    • Auto-detects common column names (tp, culprit_present, choice, etc.)
    • Recodes identification values to standard terms
    • Handles messy real-world data gracefully
    • Generates participant IDs if missing
    • Returns “lineup_data” S3 class with print method
  • create_example_lineup_data(): Generate example data for testing
    • Configurable sample size and trial distribution
    • Optional confidence ratings and response times
    • Produces realistic identification patterns
    • Useful for demonstrations and method validation
  • 76 unit tests covering validation, standardization, and integration
  • Comprehensive example script with 10 real-world scenarios

Response Time-Accuracy (RAC) Analysis

  • make_rac(): Response time-accuracy characteristic analysis
  • make_racdata(): Compute RAC data with time bins
  • make_rac_gg(): Publication-ready RAC plots
  • print.lineup_rac(): Print method for RAC objects
  • Complementary to CAC analysis for objective memory assessment
  • Follows Seale-Carlisle et al. (2019) methodology

Full ROC, EIG, and PPV-Range Analysis

  • make_fullroc() / make_fullroc_data() / plot_fullroc(): full ROC analysis using all lineup responses (Smith & Yang, 2020), with diagnosticity-ratio or a-priori ordering
  • compute_eig() / make_eig() / make_eig_data() / plot_eig(): Expected Information Gain analysis (Starns et al., 2023)
  • ppv_by_confidence() / ppv_range_by_confidence() / make_ppv_range() / plot_ppv_range(): positive predictive value across confidence levels, with nominal- and effective-size corrections

Winter 2-HT Multinomial Processing Tree Model

  • fit_winter_2ht(): two-high-threshold MPT model for the full 2x3 outcome table (Winter et al., 2022), with print(), summary(), and plot() methods
  • boot_winter_2ht(): bootstrap confidence intervals for 2-HT parameters

Calibration, ANRI, and Decision Analysis

  • make_calibration() / make_calibration_by_condition() / make_calibration_data(): confidence-accuracy calibration (C, O/U, NRI)
  • compute_anri() / bootstrap_anri() / compare_anri(): Adjusted Normalized Resolution Index with bootstrap inference
  • make_bayes_curves(), make_bree_curve(): Bayesian prior-posterior curves
  • make_utility_curves(), make_utility_difference(), compare_utility(): expected-utility analysis (Lampinen et al., 2019)
  • make_dpp(), compare_dpp(): Deviation from Perfect Performance (Smith et al., 2018)

Bayesian Beta-Binomial Inference

  • Posterior inference for core fairness measures: esize_T_bayes(), func_size_bayes(), diag_ratio_T_bayes(), calibration_bayes()
  • sdt_compare(): Bayesian comparison of SDT parameters between conditions

mSDT and MAX SDT Compound-Decision Models

  • Multi-item signal detection (mSDT) core functions: pmax_filler(), dmax_filler(), qmax_filler(), rmax_filler(), max_filler_moments(), estimate_msdt_params() (method-of-moments from rejection rates)
  • fit_max_sdt() / compare_max_sdt(): restricted aggregate Independent-Observations/MAX fitting by minimum Pearson chi-squared, with bootstrap CIs and nested-constraint comparisons

SDT Summary-Level Comparisons and GLM Estimation

  • sdt_summary_from_counts(), sdt_summary_variance(), compare_sdt_summary(): SDT comparisons when only summary counts are available (Miller/Gourevitch or bootstrap variance)
  • fit_sdt_glm() / fit_sdt_glmm() / extract_sdt_metrics(): SDT parameter estimation via probit/logit (mixed) models

Face Similarity via Deep Learning

  • face_similarity(), lineup_similarity(), batch_embeddings(), and related helpers compute facial similarity with deep embeddings (ArcFace, FaceNet, …) through Python’s deepface library (optional; requires reticulate)
  • install_r4lineups_python() / check_python_deps() for setup

Shiny App

  • run_r4lineups_app(): interactive Shiny interface to the main analyses

Core Fairness Measures

  • Bootstrap distributions for lineup bias and effective size (lineup_boot_allprop(), esize_boot_dist() and friends)
  • Data standardization is now the recommended entry point for all analyses (standardize_lineup_data())

Statistical Audit (June 2026)

A component-by-component numerical audit of the statistical routines was completed for this release. Fixes:

  • MAX SDT fitter (fit_max_sdt()): replaced the single boundary-prone optimizer start with a deterministic multistart grid plus Nelder-Mead polish; corrected the chi-square objective to use a proper outcome partition (correct-ID / filler-ID / reject); floored expected counts instead of dropping cells; corrected goodness-of-fit degrees of freedom (df = 3 x n_conditions - n_params); convergence is now reported honestly
  • Full ROC: fixed order = "apriori" with conf_bins (labels were coerced to NA, silently breaking within-decision ordering)
  • PPV: ppv_by_confidence(correction = "effective") computed the wrong effective size in the no-member-data fallback; now uses the pseudo-table counts directly
  • Calibration: added a confidence_scale = c("auto", "0-1", "0-100") argument to make_calibration_data() and all callers; auto now warns when confidence looks like a Likert/0-10 scale instead of silently dividing by 100
  • Winter 2-HT: removed the invalid single-condition goodness-of-fit chi-square test (the model is saturated, df = 0); summary() now reports a saturation note and the observed-vs-expected discrepancy as a convergence check
  • Diagnosticity ratio: fixed diagnosticity-ratio bugs and documented the Haldane correction in ln_diag_ratio()
  • Removed a duplicate internal entropy() definition that relied on file collation order
